component.name: Moonwalk
component.summary: Stream and control another computer from Linux

description.p: Moonwalk streams a remote desktop in a window or fullscreen. It sends keyboard, mouse, and gamepad input back to the host. The interface follows GNOME and KDE Plasma, and each host has its own stream settings.
Moonwalk is in alpha and designed for use on a local network. Run compatible host software on the computer you want to control.

ul.li: Discover a host, pair with a PIN, and open its Desktop entry.
Start with Automatic settings based on your display, or choose a mode for each host.
Mute sound, release input, change the view, or disconnect from the stream controls.
Copy text, images, or files when the paired host supports it.

description.p: Send the standard display request in Automatic and honor explicit command-line options. Show the host warning when it reports that the virtual display was disabled.
Keep working streams connected. Adjust bitrate where the host can do it live and save picture changes for the next connection. Apply Now reconnects at your request.
Offer takeover when a compatible host is holding a Desktop session for another device.
Check session ownership where the host can report it.
Open the main Desktop when you choose Connect.
Close HTTP connections between paired host requests.
Use a separate Remote Monitor on hosts that offer it. Reconnect to that display and close it independently of another client's app.
Keep the normal Desktop path on other hosts and send application UUIDs when available.
Find the real Desktop entry when Vibepollo also lists a running-app shortcut. Recognize titles padded for sorting.
Mask more private information in copied diagnostics and remind users to review them before sharing.
Include source license notices and clarify background cleanup and shortcuts.
Keep recent tuning results across reconnects. Check received picture sizes and return to a previous mode when a trial fails to help.
Remember when bitrate changes restart the encoder. Keep desktop geometry steady when the host cannot set UI scale.
Verify paired host state before ending a remote session and authenticate fresh TLS connections.
Return to the host list while the remote session ends in the background.
Try bitrate first, then smaller resolution steps at the same frame rate. Restore the previous mode when a trial fails to help.
Improve Desktop cleanup and recovery. Use delivered frame cadence and activity to guide Automatic.
Follow the desktop theme in stream controls, fix cursor positioning, and show negotiated video encryption. Add a way to reset learned host performance.
